caption: How a hi app works. People talk to the lead in the app's Slack channel or a DM, and send feedback from the helper on the app's pages; the lead, Hermes, helps them and files what the app's contributors, developers, and owners ask for as tasks. The owners build in the dev box, a long-lived box with the project, Claude Code, Codex, and herdr, reached over SSH or from the dev page in a browser. Work leaves the box through the app's service, part of hi on the machine: hi dev preview puts a branch on Stage, and hi dev ship merges it into dev. Production moves only when an owner or a developer releases dev from the dev page, with a snapshot first. Everything lives in the app's folder.
via: the Slack channel · the helper · the dev page

key.text: One app, one Slack channel, one machine. People reach the app through its links; owners reach the dev box over NetBird or the dev page.
The one agent that runs all the time; it talks with the people and files what they ask for, and never writes code.
Where the owners and their agents build; the agents ask no permissions, since the box is the boundary.
Part of hi, outside every box: the dev box can put work on Stage and ship through it, but nothing it offers moves production.
What the people try, and what they use. Only an owner's or a developer's click moves production.
Everything the app knows and has made, to back up, restore, or move.
